transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… it’s gotten hard for me at work. I clean buildings, and just the thought of seeing a rat—like in a trash room or an old part of the building—kind of stops me. I know it probably isn’t really dangerous, but I can’t make myself do some parts of the job anymore.
Is your fear mainly about rats?

Yeah… mainly rats. Even just thinking I might see one in a trash room or an older part of a building makes me freeze up. I know it’s probably not actually dangerous, but I still can’t make myself do parts of the job.
Do you feel your fear of rats is stronger than the actual danger they pose?
Yeah… I do. I mean, I know a rat in a trash room probably isn’t going to really hurt me, but the fear feels much bigger than that. It’s bad enough I can’t do parts of my cleaning job.
Do you go out of your way to avoid places where you might see a rat?
Yeah. I try to avoid those spots if I can… basements, storage rooms, laundry areas, alley dumpsters. If I have to go in, I leave the door open and just rush through it, scared the whole time.
Has this fear of rats been interfering with your work a lot?

Yeah… it has. I’ve had to turn down or put off some cleaning jobs in certain buildings. My supervisor’s started asking if they can really count on me for regular routes, so… I’m worried it could mess up my shifts, or any chance I had at moving up.
